item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-e418979cd781b5b3","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"López Obrador acknowledged that Alejandro Encinas was spied on but denied that the Army was responsible, told Encinas not to give the matter importance, and said nobody should be spied on; the report also described Pegasus use by military institutions against activists, journalists, and a senior human-rights official investigating alleged military abuses.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Events and presidential response reported in May 2023; the alleged Pegasus acquisition/use began in 2019.","ruler_attribution":"López Obrador made the stated denial and response; the reported surveillance was attributed by investigations to military institutions, with responsibility disputed by the president.","limitations":["The source does not establish a final independent finding on who ordered or conducted the surveillance.","The source does not report a completed investigation, discipline, remedy, or procedural correction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-06b62ec2da74f08f","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"López Obrador defended deploying 6,060 National Guard agents in the Mexico City Metro after recurrent failures and a crash that killed one student and injured 106, citing protection against possible sabotage; he dismissed human-rights criticism and defended the broader expansion of military involvement in public security.","question_ids":["2B.8","3B.2","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Deployment and justification occurred in January 2023; the accident and reported failures preceded the deployment.","ruler_attribution":"López Obrador publicly justified and defended the deployment and military role in security.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the deployment improved Metro safety or whether sabotage occurred.","The source does not describe legal authorization, oversight, proportionality review, or accountability for any misconduct."]},{"source_id":"SRC-da48ac1a48cc596e","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 reported record press violence in 2022, including 696 attacks, 12 journalist murders, 296 attacks directly perpetrated by state actors, 176 stigmatizing executive comments, concentrated discretionary government advertising, military opacity and espionage concerns, weak justice outcomes, pending institutional appointments, and partiality by the National Human Rights Commission.","question_ids":["1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.5","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in March 2023 and primarily documents conditions and events through 2022 during López Obrador’s administration.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes executive stigmatizing comments and federal resource allocation to the government; other failures involve state institutions and actors more broadly.","limitations":["The source is an advocacy organization’s assessment and does not assign personal responsibility for every reported attack or institutional failure.","Most quantitative evidence concerns 2022 rather than events occurring exclusively in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-87d371375a56ef6e","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"An FGR investigation into five civilians killed by soldiers in Nuevo Laredo found 14 bullet wounds; video appeared to show soldiers shooting unarmed men against a wall, while forensic reports were deemed consistent with the military’s shootout account despite questions about bullet trajectories and the absence of soldier injuries. López Obrador characterized the incident as isolated rather than part of an undeclared war.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","7B.1","7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The killings occurred on 18 May 2023 and the investigation/reporting continued through July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"López Obrador publicly framed the case as an isolated event; the alleged killings were attributed to soldiers, with the factual account contested.","limitations":["The source reports an ongoing investigation and conflicting evidence rather than a final judicial determination.","It does not establish whether López Obrador directed, knew of, or obstructed any unlawful conduct."]},{"source_id":"SRC-56b2c153c73612c2","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Supreme Court ruled 8–3 that transferring the National Guard’s operational, administrative, budgetary, organizational, functional, and command control to the Defense Ministry was unconstitutional because the Constitution requires a civilian institution. The government’s legislative majority was reported as respecting the decision while disagreeing with it; the article also records López Obrador’s prior measures expanding military participation in public security.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.10","4B.4","4B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The ruling occurred on 18 April 2023; the challenged transfer was enacted in September 2022 and military security authorization extended through 2028 in October 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the challenged policy to López Obrador’s administration and records the governing party’s stated respect for the Court’s ruling.","limitations":["The source does not state whether López Obrador personally complied with or sought to circumvent the ruling after the decision.","The account focuses on institutional legality rather than operational safety outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ee53fe29ecf3af8d","start_unit":20,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"Journalist Nelson Matus Peña was shot and killed by unidentified assailants in Acapulco on 15 July 2023 after reporting on crime and violence; CPJ said authorities should investigate a possible retaliatory motive and noted that the Guerrero prosecutor’s office and the federal journalist-protection mechanism did not provide information. CPJ characterized Mexican authorities as ineffective in protecting journalists and noted Mexico’s high impunity ranking.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.6","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The killing occurred in July 2023; the source reports the authorities’ response at that time and prior 2022 impunity data.","ruler_attribution":"The source does not attribute the killing to López Obrador personally, but evaluates federal and state protection and investigative institutions during his administration.","limitations":["The motive and perpetrators were unresolved in the source.","The source does not establish whether presidential directives caused or obstructed the investigation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ac74e81f4e211be7","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that Mexican authorities used disproportionate criminal proceedings, vague offenses, stigmatization, harassment, excessive force, and threats against peaceful land, territorial, and environmental defenders, including people opposing a National Guard barracks; it said authorities failed to investigate abuses and recommended ending criminalization, strengthening protection, and avoiding militarized forces to monitor protests.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.7","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7","7B.10","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in September 2023 and describes cases and practices during the period of López Obrador’s administration.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to various Mexican state authorities and specifically criticizes use of the National Guard in protest monitoring; it does not allege personal presidential direction in each case.","limitations":["The source is an Amnesty International report and does not quantify nationwide prevalence.","The source does not document a presidential response to each case or recommendation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9bbcbadcb4a780c8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A federal judge suspended Maya Train Section 5 construction because the government lacked required land-use authorization; the project had previously faced suspensions for missing environmental-impact authorization and was restarted while lacking an explicit judicial order after being designated a national-security project. Environmental authorities identified critical impacts including more than 485 hectares of deforestation, cave-system damage, altered water flows, and risks to jaguars; the government announced a 2,249-hectare jaguar reserve.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.6","3B.4","3B.7","4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10","7B.2","7B.7","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The reported suspension occurred in February 2023; prior authorization disputes and the government’s environmental response are included for context.","ruler_attribution":"The project was an López Obrador administration priority; government agencies resumed or defended construction and announced the jaguar reserve.","limitations":["The source does not establish the final environmental outcome or whether the reserve offset project impacts.","The report does not provide the complete legal record or quantify final compliance after the suspension."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6219fd63396b6214","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"López Obrador accelerated and personally supervised major projects for planned 2023 inaugurations, including the Tulum airport, Maya Train, Interoceanic Corridor, and an Army-run medicine distribution center; the projects involved large public investments and military construction or administration. Critics questioned symbolic inaugurations before completion and the timing near the 2024 election, citing the delayed operation of the Dos Bocas refinery.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.2","6B.4","6B.9","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Plans, supervision, and reported implementation status concern late 2023.","ruler_attribution":"López Obrador set the deadlines, supervised works, and presented the projects as central government priorities; Sedena handled some construction and operations.","limitations":["Several outcomes were projected rather than completed at the time of reporting.","The article does not provide independent cost-effectiveness, distributional, or service-quality evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7c25acd80b4c3cda","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Morena-majority Budget Commission proposed 13.262 billion pesos in cuts to Congress, the judiciary, INE, Auditoría Superior, Cofece, and INAI for 2024, including reductions of 6.465 billion to the judiciary and 5.003 billion to the electoral authority, while increasing allocations to executive ministries and Pemex. A proposed Otis-recovery fund was not included in the distributed budget draft.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.10","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","6B.6","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The proposal was reported in November 2023 for the 2024 budget.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the proposal to the Morena-majority commission and reports it in the context of López Obrador’s proposal to redirect judicial-fund resources.","limitations":["The article reports a commission proposal before final budget approval.","It does not establish that López Obrador personally ordered each specific reduction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7144fb962f70af0d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"During López Obrador’s first four years, information requests increased, but complaints over inadequate or denied responses rose 19% compared with the prior administration; authorities frequently cited nonexistent information or national-security classification. INAI became unable to meet because it had only four of seven commissioners after López Obrador vetoed two Senate-approved nominees, while Morena blocked further appointments.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The data cover the first four years of López Obrador’s administration and were reported in April 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes criticism of INAI and the veto of two nominees to López Obrador, and appointment blockage to Morena in the Senate.","limitations":["The complaint data concern all Mexican authorities, not only the executive.","The source reports political attribution but does not establish the legal reasons for the vetoes or the president’s stated intent."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus is concentrated on security, militarization, press freedom, institutional checks, transparency, infrastructure, and protest; it provides little or no direct evidence for nuclear, arms-control, foreign-war, macroeconomic, health-service, welfare-distribution, or personal-financial-integrity questions.","Facts are limited to what the supplied documents report and are not scores or final causal findings."]}
